summary: Junko Matsumura is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at the Australian National University (MA, 1980) and the University of Göttingen (doctoral dissertation, 1990), and was attested as a professor at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies in 2011.
Junko Minamoto works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Ryukoku University and Otani University (around 1976–1980) and held a research post at Kansai University.

Junsho Kato is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo, KU Leuven, and under Étienne Lamotte, Juntaka Kato, Akira Hirakawa, and Hajime Nakamura. He served as professor at Nishogakusha University and Nagoya University.

Juntarō Ishihama worked in Sinology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Kansai University and held posts at Ryukoku University (around 1922–1948) and Kansai University (around 1949–1968).
Junzo Inagaki is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He studied under Shoshin Fukihara and served as a section head at the Otani University Library.
Juri Lotman was a linguist who completed multiple periods of study at Saint Petersburg State University between 1939 and 1961. He joined the faculty of the University of Tartu in 1954.
Juro Watanabe works in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Gerhard Oberhammer and held an attested post at the University of Tsukuba from 1989 to 1990.

Justin McDaniel works in Buddhist and religious studies. He has held posts as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at the University of California, Riverside, and Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Pennsylvania (attested 2011–2018).

Justin Ritzinger is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Harvard University under Robert M. Gimello and Michael Puett, and held posts at Oberlin College, Dharma Drum Mountain, and Academia Sinica.
Justin Shimeld is a philosopher. He completed his PhD at the University of Tasmania under the supervision of Jeff Malpas and Sonam Thakchoe (attested 2012).
Justus Günther Grassmann studied at the Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (around 1798–1801) and held a post at the Marienstiftsgymnasium from 1806 to 1852.

Justus Olshausen worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at Kiel University, Paris, and Berlin, learning under Silvestre de Sacy. He held posts at Kiel University, the University of Königsberg, and the Prussian Ministry.
Jyotirindranath Tagore was an Indian scholar active in linguistics who studied at the Hindu School and Presidency University (around 1864).

János Szerb was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. After studying at Eötvös Loránd University, he held posts at the University of Vienna (1982) and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (around 1985–1988).
Jérôme Ducor is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied under Jacques May (around 1984–1992) and held an attested post at the University of Lausanne around 1999.

Józef Szczepan Kowalewski was a scholar of Mongolian, Buddhist, and Iranian studies. He studied at Vilnius University and Kazan Federal University, later serving as professor and rector at Kazan (1833–1860) and professor and dean at the University of Warsaw.
Józef Turczyński held posts at the Ukrainian National Academy of Music (around 1915–1919) and the Chopin University of Music (around 1920–1939), and taught Constantin Régamey.

József Budenz was a linguist who studied under Theodor Benfey at the University of Göttingen and at the University of Marburg. He served at the Hungarian Academy of Sciences and as professor at Eötvös Loránd University (1868–1892).

Jörg Heimbel is a Tibetologist who studied at Tibet University and earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Dorji Wangchuk and Franz-Karl Ehrhard. He became a Tibetan lecturer at the University of Hamburg (attested 2019).
Jörg Plassen is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He has held posts as a professor at Geumgang University and at Ruhr University Bochum (attested 2013).
